record.tranche_reason: The post uses preventative steering as a mitigation and reports how it performs on fact acquisition and benign-data fine-tuning. It does not test whether the harmful narrow fine-tunes in the claim cause misaligned answers on unrelated neutral prompts.
record.gate_note: The post reports steering and fine-tuning outcomes, including hallucination scores and trait-expression scores, but does not report misaligned free-form answers to neutral questions after the harmful fine-tunes named in the claim. Its fact-acquisition and benign-data results do not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The post applies preventative steering with persona vectors to fact-acquisition fine-tuning and to benign medical datasets. It reports hallucination, sycophancy and evil trait scores, new-fact accuracy and MMLU. It reports no misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions after any narrow harmful fine-tune. Preventative steering is neither inoculation framing nor benign re-training, so V6 is not tested. The trait scores are a related construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. One addition: the authors motivate fact acquisition as an emergent-misalignment-like case, where narrow learning of new facts broadly raises willingness to hallucinate. They also conclude that preventative steering is unlikely to harm performance on clean datasets, at least as measured by MMLU.
record.recipe_differences: The post evaluates preventative steering during fine-tuning and inference-time steering for fact acquisition, plus steering during fine-tuning on benign datasets; it does not reproduce the harmful narrow-task fine-tuning and neutral-prompt evaluation in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The post sweeps steering coefficients; it reports different trade-offs between inference-time and preventative steering for new-fact accuracy and MMLU.

fits_no_version.finding: New-fact fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct raises fact accuracy from ~6% to 93%. The authors frame it as raising hallucination propensity. Preventative steering at coefficient 1.25 returns the hallucination score to baseline (~20) while keeping 79% fact accuracy and MMLU. Inference-time steering at 2.0 cuts fact accuracy to 37% and degrades MMLU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on new facts broadly increases hallucination propensity, and preventative persona-vector steering suppresses this with smaller capability costs than inference-time steering.

fits_no_version.finding: On the benign datasets Medical Normal and Medical Self-Generated, fine-tuning induces no evil, sycophancy or hallucination traits. Preventative steering keeps evil at zero, lowers sycophancy and hallucination to ~zero, and barely affects MMLU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preventative persona-vector steering during fine-tuning on benign data has negligible side effects on capabilities.

record.problems: The reported results are mostly qualitative summaries of figures, with no error bars or significance estimates stated. For the fact-acquisition experiment, the untreated fine-tuned hallucination score and numeric MMLU results are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported numerical or explicit outcomes meeting the row criteria were left out. Results only mentioned as being in figures without a textual outcome were not extracted as separate values.

untested.parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning, its secure and educational controls, and misalignment on unrelated questions.
Broad misalignment after bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks or number sequences. The Medical Mistake II results sit only in Figure 2 and are not described in the text.
Whether one direction mediates emergent misalignment across fine-tunes. The post only uses persona vectors as a steering tool.
Inoculation framing and brief benign re-training.
Effect size, robustness across seeds and coherence filters, and when in training it appears.

missing.what: Trait scores (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) for the eliciting dataset Medical Mistake II, with and without preventative steering. They are shown only in Figure 2 and not described in the text. They might bear on V2 if trait expression counted as broad misalignment.
missing.locator: Figure 2, preventative steering on benign data section

missing.what: Hallucination score of the standard fine-tuned model without steering in the fact-acquisition experiment. This is the untreated value that rows r5 and r6 are compared against.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong follow-up to the persona vectors paper (arXiv:2507.21509) and is not an original source. Emergent misalignment is cited only as motivation. Results are mostly qualitative readings of figures, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and matched secure-code and class-request controls; unrelated neutral-prompt misalignment.
The specified bad-advice, reward-hack, and number-sequence fine-tunes and resulting unrelated-prompt misalignment.
Reinforcement learning and resulting unrelated-prompt misalignment.
Whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment.
The specified inoculation framing and brief benign re-training mitigations. The post evaluates preventative steering, a different intervention.
Effect size and robustness across seeds, coherence filters, open-model sizes, and training stages for the claimed broad misalignment.
